To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the gender dimensions of the effects of economic reforms on female paid employment, household work and leisure are complex and varied.
trade liberalization in the absence as in the presence, of compensatory measures leads to an increase in female market work, and fiscal adjustment reduces it.
trade liberalisation increases female employment in the market, but the increase in female leisure time is not significant.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of economic reform on the allocation of time between market work, household work and leisure for women and men.
the impact of economic reform on the gender division of labor in Pakistan.
the impact of economic policies on the time allocation of men and women in Pakistan.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
economic reforms in the form of trade liberalisation and fiscal adjustment increase women's paid employment but decrease women's leisure time.
trade liberalisation increases female paid employment, but the increase in demand for market goods reduces female leisure time and does not change female household work.
economic reforms, especially trade liberalisation, lead to a rise in female paid employment, but at the expense of leisure time, and to a lesser extent, household time.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the gendered CGE model is a useful tool for gender analysis, as it provides information about the impact of economic policy on gender dimensions of time allocation.
the gendered computable general equilibrium model is a useful tool for analysing the gender dimensions of the economic reforms.
trade liberalisation increases the demand for female labour and leads to an overall increase in female paid employment, but it also increases female leisure time.
The main takeaway from our work is that
trade liberalisation and fiscal adjustment both reduce gender inequality.
economic reforms in Pakistan have a positive effect on female labour force participation, and the impact is higher in the presence of fiscal adjustment.
trade and fiscal reforms have gendered effects on time allocation among market, household, leisure activities.
